structure.note: Share capital of €911 million: 455,500,000 unlisted ordinary (voting) shares and 455,500,000 listed non-voting preferred shares, each with a €1 notional share of capital; preferred shares get a €0.01 higher dividend. Volkswagen AG indirectly holds 75% of the ordinary shares less one share (via Porsche Holding Stuttgart GmbH) and Porsche Automobil Holding SE holds 25% plus one share. Of the preferred shares, 75.8% are indirectly held by Volkswagen AG and 24.2% are free float. As a percentage of share capital: Volkswagen AG 75.4%, Porsche SE 12.5%, institutional and private investors 12.1%.

notes: All figures from the Porsche AG Annual and Sustainability Report 2024 (consolidated financial statements, IFRS), fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, on investorrelations.porsche.com. EUR, converted exactly from € millions. OWNERSHIP: the report does not disclose Oliver Blume's personal holding of Porsche AG shares (no shareholding table or share ownership guideline holding found), so status is 'not-disclosed'. The holder percentages are of total share capital (ordinary plus preferred), as the chart states, so they are economic. Volkswagen's 75.4% and Porsche SE's 12.5% are separate holdings and do not overlap within Porsche AG. Qatar or other preferred-share holders are not disclosed in this report. DIVIDENDS: €2,100 million paid to Porsche AG shareholders (statement of changes in equity); the cash-flow line 'Profit transfer and dividends' of €2,101 million includes €1 million to non-controlling interests. BUYBACKS: 0. The cash-flow statement has no line for purchases of own shares and the report describes no share buyback or treasury shares. STOCK COMP: null. Porsche AG's share-based payment (note 43) consists of cash-settled virtual performance share plans for the Executive Board and management and an IPO bonus; no shares are granted. The note gives the expense in parts (a table for the Executive Board and top management, and 'a total expense of €37 million' for other members of management, plus the IPO bonus) without a company-wide total, so no figure is recorded rather than summing. GEOGRAPHY: the five regions as reported; the 'Hedges sales revenue' column of €–4 million is omitted, so the segments sum to €40,087 million against the Group total of €40,083 million.

footprint.notes: Porsche reports deliveries and employees by its five sales regions; Germany is a region and a country, so it is stored as a country row (DE), once per metric. Only 'China incl. Hong Kong' carries a country list because the report names its members; 'North America excl. Mexico', 'Europe without Germany' and 'Overseas and Emerging Markets' (the remaining countries; renamed from 'rest of the world') are left null. Each region appears twice, once per metric, because deliveries and employees come from different passages. The employee table's column headers (Germany | Europe (without Germany) | North America excl. Mexico | China incl. Hong Kong | Overseas and emerging markets | Total) map to the values in order; the quote joins the table title and row with '…'. No per-country delivery figures (e.g. U.S.) appear in the report or the Jan 2025 deliveries release, and no U.S. state data. Documents are the English PDFs on newsroom.porsche.com (Porsche notes only the German version is legally binding). Bratislava, Osnabrück and Kulim are Volkswagen Group or third-party sites used by Porsche, not Porsche-owned plants.
